definition.simple: Atoms of DIFFERENT elements that surprisingly have the EXACT SAME weight.
definition.academic: Atoms of different chemical elements that have the same number of nucleons (same mass number) but differ in atomic number.

examples: Argon (atomic number 18) and Calcium (atomic number 20) both have a mass number of 40. They are isobars.

common_misconceptions: Isobars have the same properties. (False: They are entirely different elements, so they have completely different properties).
ai_context.tutor_hint: To remember Isobars vs Isotopes: IsoBARS have the same mass (think of a heavy barbell!).
